questions.stem: A service tags each snapshot with hash() of its JSON text and keeps the tags in a table shared by four worker processes, each started normally. Another worker looks up yesterday's snapshot by the same text. What happens?

options.text: It finds the snapshot, since hash() of equal text is equal in every process
options.says: Only within one process: the salt for str hashes is drawn anew in each process.

options.text: It misses the snapshot, since each process salts the hash of a string itself
options.says: Right: the lesson's two processes gave different hash() values for the same text and the same SHA-256.

options.text: It finds the snapshot, since a fixed hash seed is the default in a process
options.says: The default is a random salt; a fixed seed has to be set with PYTHONHASHSEED.

options.text: It misses the snapshot, since hash() of an integer tag is salted per process
options.says: Integer hashes are not salted (hash(2030) was 2030 in both processes); the salt applies to str and bytes.

origin.section: hash() Is Salted per Process, So It Cannot Name a Snapshot

questions.stem: A team's canonical form sorts every list in a snapshot before hashing. Two snapshots are identical except that one project's two-year cost profile is reversed. What do their digests show?

options.text: Different digests, since sorting keeps each cost profile in its order
options.says: Sorting reorders the profile; reversed and original sort to the same list.

options.text: Different digests, since each list sorts into a new order of its own
options.says: Two lists with the same values sort to the same order, so the bytes agree.

options.text: Equal digests, although the snapshots describe two different projects
options.says: Right: the order of a cost profile is its meaning, so sorting it makes different content look equal.

options.text: Equal digests, since the snapshots describe one and the same project
options.says: A project that spends 880 then 1,170 is not the project that spends 1,170 then 880.

origin.section: Hash the Validated Content in Canonical Form, Not the File

questions.stem: A stored snapshot, named by its digest, is edited in place to fix one budget. The store re-hashes each file when it reads it. What happens on the next read, and what was the right way to make the fix?

options.text: The read returns the fix; a small edit in place is fine for such a fix
options.says: The re-hash no longer matches the name, so the read is refused.

options.text: The read is refused; the fix belongs in a new version with its own digest
options.says: Right: put the new content, which gets a new digest and version and leaves the old one intact.

options.text: The read is refused; the fix belongs in the old file under its old name
options.says: That is the edit in place that was just refused: content and name must agree.

options.text: The read returns the old data; the store keeps a copy of each file it holds
options.says: The store keeps one file per digest; the edited file is all it has, and it is refused.

origin.section: A Snapshot Is Stored Once Under Its Digest and Checked Again on Every Read
